title: EHR operations overview
question: Choose the composition that should lead the EHR. Each option keeps the confirmed operations-overview purpose and the existing Ovok purple design system. Lock one, and mention anything that feels wrong or should be combined.

options.label: Daily clinic rounds
options.thesis: Today's work stays together on one operational sheet.
options.viewport: Clinic navigation anchors a work sheet led by today's follow-ups and appointments; a narrow line of labeled counts summarizes intake, assignment, enrollment, and kit availability; patient rows open the canonical chart.
options.risk: The overview can become a metric dashboard if the work queue loses priority.

options.label: Enrollment workbench
options.thesis: Every unfinished RPM enrollment is visible as a patient journey.
options.viewport: An operations overview keeps clinic totals compact and puts in-progress patient lanes first: intake, clinician, CHF plan, questionnaire, and physical device assignment each show an owner and next action.
options.risk: An enrollment-first layout can hide appointments and routine follow-up work.

options.label: Patient review register
options.thesis: The patient list itself becomes the clinic's clear next-action index.
options.viewport: A fast patient search sits above a dense but readable register; each row shows assignment, enrollment state, latest ECG/weight/questionnaire source time, and a chart action, with operations counts in the heading band.
options.risk: A register can read like measurement review instead of a full operations overview.

options.label: Split-flap clinic queue
options.lineage: A station departure board's fixed columns and changing rows
options.thesis: Clinic work becomes a glanceable queue with patient context in every row.
materials: high-contrast text within the Ovok palette
options.viewport: The patient work queue is a stable table whose status and latest-reading cells update without moving its columns.
options.case: Competitive: stateful rows and fixed columns suit quick scanning, but the station-board framing is less familiar than clinic handover.
options.risk: Patient care can look like operational telemetry if the table overwhelms the patient context.
